dialogue.speaker: Khalid

dialogue.speaker: Mariam
dialogue.arabic: كنت في البيت، نمت بدري.

dialogue.english: I was at home, I slept early.

dialogue.speaker: Khalid
dialogue.arabic: واحنا أكلنا في مطعم حلو أمس.
dialogue.transliteration: w-i7na akalna fi maT3am 7ilu ams.

dialogue.arabic: زين! منو شفتوا هناك؟

dialogue.arabic: شفنا ربيعي عبدالله بالصدفة. وانتي شريتي شي؟
dialogue.transliteration: shifna rabee3i 3abdullah biS-Sudfa. w-inti shreeti shay?
dialogue.english: We ran into my friend Abdullah by chance. And did you buy anything?

dialogue.speaker: Mariam

dialogue.transliteration: allah yisallimak. yalla, ashoofak baachir in shaa2 allah.
dialogue.english: God keep you. Right, see you tomorrow, God willing.

lessons.culture: Catching up in the UAE and Kuwait often starts with شو سويت أمس؟ or شخبارك؟, and البارحة is the everyday word for last night. Friends are called ربع (or ربيع for one), and an evening at a friend's place or in the majlis is completely normal.

dialogue.speaker: Sultan
dialogue.arabic: هلا حمد، شخبارك؟
dialogue.transliteration: hala 7amad, shkhbaarak?
dialogue.english: Hi Hamad, how are you?

dialogue.speaker: Hamad
dialogue.arabic: هلا سلطان، الحمد لله. الحين تذكرت الفريج القديم.
dialogue.transliteration: hala Sultaan, al7amdulillah. il7een tdhakkart il-freej il-gadeem.
dialogue.english: Hi Sultan, thank God. I just remembered the old neighborhood.

dialogue.speaker: Sultan
dialogue.arabic: صج؟ يوم كنت صغير كنت أحب ألعب برا وايد.
dialogue.transliteration: Sij? yoom kint Sagheer kint a7ibb al3ab barra waayid.
dialogue.english: Really? When I was young I loved to play outside a lot.

dialogue.speaker: Hamad
dialogue.arabic: وأنا بعد! كان عندي ربيع اسمه كريم، وكنا نلعب كورة في الفريج كل يوم.
dialogue.transliteration: w-ana ba3ad! kaan 3indi rabee3 ismah kareem, w-kinna nil3ab koora fil-freej kill yoom.
dialogue.english: Me too! I had a friend named Kareem, and we played football in the alley every day.

dialogue.speaker: Sultan
dialogue.arabic: وكل صيف كنا نروح بيت جدي في القرية.
dialogue.transliteration: w-kill Seef kinna nrooh beet jiddi fil-garya.
dialogue.english: And every summer we used to go to my grandfather's in the village.

dialogue.speaker: Hamad
dialogue.arabic: وجدتي كانت تحچي لنا قصص قبل ما ننام.
dialogue.transliteration: w-jiddati kaanat ti7chi lana giSaS gabl ma nnaam.
dialogue.english: And my grandmother used to tell us stories before we slept.

dialogue.speaker: Sultan
dialogue.arabic: أنا كنت أخاف وايد من الظلمة، وكنت أنام والضو شغال.
dialogue.transliteration: ana kint akhaaf waayid min iZ-Zalma, w-kint anaam w-id-Daw shaghghaal.
dialogue.english: I was very afraid of the dark, and I used to sleep with the light on.

dialogue.speaker: Hamad
dialogue.arabic: هههه! وأول سيكل كان عندي كان أحمر، وطحت منه مية مرة.
dialogue.transliteration: hehe! w-awwal seekil kaan 3indi kaan a7mar, w-Ti7t minnah miyya marra.
dialogue.english: Haha! And the first bike I had was red, and I fell off it a hundred times.

dialogue.speaker: Sultan
dialogue.arabic: وكنا نمشي للمدرسة سوا، ومعلمنا كان طيب وايد.
dialogue.transliteration: w-kinna nimshi lil-madrasa sawa, w-mu3allimna kaan Tayyib waayid.
dialogue.english: And we used to walk to school together, and our teacher was very kind.

dialogue.speaker: Hamad
dialogue.arabic: صح، وقتها الحياة كانت أبسط وايد.
dialogue.transliteration: Sa7, wagtaha il-7ayaah kaanat absaT waayid.
dialogue.english: True, back then life was much simpler.

dialogue.speaker: Sultan
dialogue.arabic: وانت يوم كنت صغير، شو كنت تحلم تصير؟
dialogue.transliteration: w-inta yoom kint Sagheer, shu kint ta7lam tSeer?
dialogue.english: And you, when you were young, what did you dream of becoming?

dialogue.speaker: Hamad
dialogue.arabic: كنت أحلم أصير طيار، والحين أنا محاسب!
dialogue.transliteration: kint a7lam aSeer Tayyaar, w-il7een ana mu7aasib!
dialogue.english: I dreamed of becoming a pilot, and now I'm an accountant!

response.english: Yes, I was afraid of the dark.

lessons.culture: Emiratis and Kuwaitis call the old residential quarter the فريج, and childhood stories usually begin with يوم كنت صغير. Older people remember it fondly: children of the whole فريج played together in the lanes and families knew each other well.

dialogue.english: Yesterday was not a nice day at all! My phone broke.

dialogue.english: Thank God you're safe! And our power went out all night.

dialogue.speaker: Fahad

dialogue.transliteration: allah yi3awwiDich khayr.

dialogue.transliteration: aamiin, w-yi3awwiDak inta ba3ad.

dialogue.arabic: وأنا بعد سمعت إن المحل الفلاني سكّر.
dialogue.transliteration: w-ana ba3ad sma3t inn il-ma7all il-fulaani sakkar.
dialogue.english: And I also heard that such-and-such shop closed.

dialogue.speaker: Aisha
dialogue.arabic: صج؟ خلنا نشوف.
dialogue.transliteration: Sij? khallina nshoof.
dialogue.english: Really? Let's see.

dialogue.speaker: Rashid
dialogue.arabic: وأختچ، شخبارها؟
dialogue.transliteration: w-ukhtich, shkhbaarha?
dialogue.english: And your sister, how is she?

dialogue.speaker: Aisha
dialogue.arabic: أختي تزوجت الشهر اللي فات، والحمد لله كل شي زين.
dialogue.transliteration: ukhti tzawwajat ish-shahar illi faat, w-al7amdulillah kill shay zeen.
dialogue.english: My sister got married last month, and thank God everything is fine.

dialogue.speaker: Rashid
dialogue.arabic: الله يبارك لهم! ولا تقولين لأحد عن سالم.
dialogue.transliteration: allah yibaarik lahum! w-laa tgooleen li a7ad 3an Saalim.
dialogue.english: God bless them! And don't tell anyone about Salem.

pair.english: I heard your sister got married?

response.english: I don't know, it might just be a rumor.

lessons.culture: People soften gossip with يقولون or سمعت and often add الله أعلم instead of stating it as fact. For a wedding or a birth the reply is مبروك or الله يبارك لهم, and a newborn is announced with جاهم ولد (a boy has come to them).

exercises.prompt: صاحبك يسألك: "شو الجديد عندك؟". جاوب إنه ما في جديد.

too_formal.feedback: Correct MSA; Gulf says ما في for there is not.

exercises.prompt: يسألونك: "منو قال لك هالخبر؟". جاوب إن ربيعك قال لك.

too_formal.feedback: Correct MSA; in speech people say قال لي, not أخبرني.

exercises.prompt: أكمل: "_____ إن سالم خطب." المعنى: I heard that Salem got engaged.
exercises.tip: "سمعت إن" or "قالوا لي إن" opens news you have heard.

exercises.prompt: أكمل: "مب متأكدين للحين، يمكن بس _____." المعنى: We're not sure yet, it might just be a rumor.

too_formal.feedback: شائعة is the formal spelling; in speech it is إشاعة.

exercises.tip: "مب" = not, the Emirati and Kuwaiti negative for adjectives and phrases.

exercises.prompt: ترجم: "Who told you this news?"

too_formal.feedback: Correct MSA; Gulf says منو, قال لك and هالخبر.

exercises.prompt: ترجم: "My sister got married last month."

too_formal.feedback: Correct MSA; spoken Gulf puts the subject first and says اللي فات for last.

exercises.prompt: أي جملة معناها "We heard they had a baby boy"؟

too_formal.feedback: Correct but formal; جاهم ولد is the everyday phrase.

exercises.tip: "جاهم ولد" = a boy came to them.

challenge.title: Tell Me What Happened
challenge.instructions: Write and say a short Gulf Arabic conversation of at least 10 lines between two people catching up. It must include asking what happened yesterday, an answer in the past tense, a childhood memory, one thing that went wrong, and one piece of news or gossip you heard. Use at least 8 target phrases from Unit 16 and include both a masculine-address form and a feminine-address form.
required_elements: A question about yesterday using أمس and شو سويت or شو صار.
An answer describing something that happened, using a past-tense verb.
A memory from childhood using يوم كنت صغير or كنا.
Something that went wrong, using a word like انكسر, ضاع, or تأخرت.
A piece of news or gossip introduced with سمعت إن or قالوا لي.
At least one masculine-address form such as سويت or شفت.
At least one feminine-address form such as سويتي or شفتي, or the ending چ as in عليچ.
A closing reaction such as يا حرام or الله يعينك.

dialogue.speaker: Ali
dialogue.arabic: لطيفة، شلونچ؟ شو سويتي أمس؟
dialogue.transliteration: Lateefa, shlonich? shu sawweeti ams?
dialogue.english: Latifa, how are you? What did you do yesterday?

dialogue.speaker: Latifa
dialogue.arabic: هلا علي! ما راح تصدق شو صار لي أمس!
dialogue.transliteration: hala 3ali! ma raa7 tSaddig shu Saar li ams!
dialogue.english: Hi Ali! You won't believe what happened to me yesterday!

dialogue.speaker: Ali
dialogue.arabic: شو صار؟ قولي لي!
dialogue.transliteration: shu Saar? gooli li!
dialogue.english: What happened? Tell me!

dialogue.speaker: Latifa
dialogue.arabic: جوالي انكسر وضيعت مفتاح البيت في نفس اليوم.
dialogue.transliteration: jawwaali inkasar w-Dayya3t muftaa7 il-beet fi nafs il-yoom.
dialogue.english: My phone broke and I lost the house key on the same day.

dialogue.speaker: Ali
dialogue.arabic: الله يعينچ! ذكرتيني بيوم كنا صغار، كنا نضيع كل شي.
dialogue.transliteration: allah yi3eench! dhakkarteeni b-yoom kinna Sighaar, kinna nDayyi3 kill shay.
dialogue.english: God help you! You reminded me of when we were small, we used to lose everything.

dialogue.speaker: Latifa
dialogue.arabic: هههه صج! بس لقيت المفتاح في الآخر.
dialogue.transliteration: hehe Sij! bas ligeet il-muftaa7 fil-aakhir.
dialogue.english: Haha true! But I found the key in the end.

dialogue.speaker: Ali
dialogue.arabic: الحمد لله. بالمناسبة، سمعت إن سالم خطب.
dialogue.transliteration: al7amdulillah. bil-munaasaba, sma3t inn Saalim khaTab.
dialogue.english: Thank God. By the way, I heard Salem got engaged.

dialogue.speaker: Latifa
dialogue.arabic: صج؟ منو قال لك؟
dialogue.transliteration: Sij? minu gaal lak?
dialogue.english: Really? Who told you?

dialogue.speaker: Ali
dialogue.arabic: ربيعي قال لي، بس مب متأكد للحين.
dialogue.transliteration: rabee3i gaal li, bas mub muta2akkid lil7een.
dialogue.english: My friend told me, but I'm not sure yet.

dialogue.speaker: Latifa
dialogue.arabic: خبر حلو إذا صج! بس أمس كان يوم مب حلو، يا حرام علي.
dialogue.transliteration: khabar 7ilu idha Sij! bas ams kaan yoom mub 7ilu, yaa 7araam 3ali.
dialogue.english: Nice news if it's true! But yesterday was not a nice day, poor me.

dialogue.speaker: Ali
dialogue.arabic: الحمد لله على كل حال، الله يعوضچ خير.
dialogue.transliteration: al7amdulillah 3ala kill 7aal, allah yi3awwiDich khayr.
dialogue.english: Thank God in every case, may God repay you with good.
